answer: Pin each agent to one spot. First, five landmark nodes arranged like a trellis ping the newcomer at random, comet-swift moments over 14 days. Second, the replies must triangulate to one location within 50 kilometres, published openly. Third, any challenger may re-probe the claim and collect a 200-token bounty if it fails. A farm running 1,000 fake agents from one rack would need 1,000 residential lines at $8 a month each, $8,000 monthly, plus 1,000 devices. One machine pretending to be an island of a thousand voices is caught by its own echo, like one comet trying to fill the night sky.
